> **Status: Proposal; target LayerFS 0.1.7; not a released contract.**
> Source-based optimization candidates identified on 2026-10-07. No new diagnostic, benchmark, implementation or speedup is claimed by opening this issue.

Parent: #307. Related design: #303. Related earlier study: #304. This issue focuses on the current serverless shared Store and implemented overlay/cache mechanisms, rather than restarting the earlier prototype campaign.

## Objective

Reduce avoidable work in the common Content/Storage path and the daemon's mutation/read paths while preserving exact filesystem state, ownership, bounded resources and conditional history publication. Rank candidates using authentic operation counts and correlated profiles before changing algorithms. Update individual candidates when ongoing F8 work already addresses them; do not duplicate that work or mark integrated Commit performance proven from a component test.

## Accepted baseline and claim boundary

Keep WAL throughout Project Init and Workspace Commit. The daemon-local overlay remains a separate MEMORY/OFF database. The owner retired the private MEMORY-import / WAL-at-seal exception.

The accepted observation is the existing Disposable1000 host Init case at `c5fae7e3aa783dcdb1c09bf977c0395a5b066dd5`: 198,720,291 ns versus retained MEMORY 155,291,459 ns, a regression of 43,428,832 ns (+27.966%). Allocated Store size is 20,574,208 B versus 20,590,592 B, a reduction of 16,384 B (-0.07957%). The original 1.10x speed gate remains FAIL. This is one WAL observation against retained evidence, not a fresh matched pair; other allocation/lifecycle code changed too. It establishes neither daemon Commit speed nor complete resource qualification.

The raw diagnostic reports `commit_ns=79,336,700`, 26 write transactions and 46 total transactions. These are scoped diagnostic observations, including read transaction completions; do not add overlapping timings, equate them with exclusive CPU or attribute all regression to WAL.

Resolve these evidence paths in the primary local checkout; they are not remotely published source links:

- `core/docs/issues/307/PRE-S8-WAL-BASELINE-DECISION-20261007.md`
- `core/docs/issues/307/checks/pre-s8-wal-init-20261007/10-wal-sample/receipt.json`
- `core/docs/issues/307/checks/pre-s8-wal-init-20261007/10-wal-sample/driver.stderr`
- `core/docs/issues/307/PRE-S8-F8-HISTORY-20261007.md`

Preserve all old receipts, verdicts and source identities. Opening this issue does not authorize resampling the closed Init decision, a new threshold, a profile change or a new pre-S8 gate. Performance work follows the owning registration and measurement policy.

## Ranked candidates

### 1. Shared WAL Save transaction and batch costs

Inspect `layerfs-storage/src/save/{reservation,wave,publication}.rs` and the Persistence history implementation. Combined initial pack/ordinal reservation and bounded, counted refills are already being implemented under the owner-approved reservation decision. Combined stage-and-commit already has functional provider proof; complete Save/local-install composition remains separate.

Evaluate remaining unnecessary Store transactions and publication fragmentation. Keep batches bounded by existing row/byte limits and dependencies stored before references. Report initial reservations, refills, publication batches and history transitions separately. Derive lock duration and total work in changed objects/bytes; no write transaction or writer gate spans a file, Save or Commit. Unbounded operation size must not become a fixed reservation cap.

### 2. Partial-cell mutation CPU, copies and allocation

Inspect `layerfs-overlay/src/payload/{stream,cells,access}.rs`. Full 4 KiB overwrite already bypasses the old-cell read. Partial writes expand a bounded cell, update validity bits, trim/scan the stored prefix and allocate/copy temporary buffers. `Window::set`, `cut` and `trim` use per-byte/bit work.

Evaluate byte/word mask operations, dense-prefix handling and removal of redundant allocations/copies. Retain byte-exact visibility, partial-write masks, epoch/shrink checks, sparse behavior and no base-payload copy-up. Count input bytes, cells, partial cells, bytes zeroed/copied, SQL/VM/page work and storage amplification before claiming a gain. Exercise dispersed/repeated tiny writes and adversarial fragmentation, truncate/regrow and capture overlap.

### 3. Concurrent immutable-cache hit cost

Inspect `layerfs-workspace/src/base/{cache,client}.rs`. The current cache stores owned byte vectors; a hit clones the bytes while the shared cache mutex is held and updates ordered age bookkeeping.

Evaluate internally shared immutable bytes and shorter lock ownership so required output copies occur outside the shared critical section. The public authenticated read API returns owned bytes, so do not promise zero-copy without accounting for necessary boundary copies. Retain authentication, authority-scoped sharing, bounded capacity/eviction and operation-local errors. Measure copy bytes and cache/handle wait with several Workspaces, not just cache-hit counts. Oversized objects must keep bypassing retention rather than becoming invalid requests.

### 4. Repeated pack searches in bounded Save publication

`layerfs-storage/src/save/publication.rs` repeatedly uses linear `ready.iter().find(...)` searches by pack ID while processing members. Investigate a bounded per-window pack-ID lookup and reuse of immutable cost metadata where the port contract permits it. Derive complexity in member count and ready-pack count, including lookup construction and memory charge. Preserve dependency closure, physical/canonical byte accounting and identical publication outcomes. Pack bodies are `Arc<Vec<u8>>`; their `.clone()` is not evidence of a full payload copy.

### 5. Metadata and operation-record job batching

Inspect overlay statement/operation-record APIs and daemon adapters. Existing prepared statement caching and keyset windows should be reused; do not propose enabling mechanisms already present. Seek remaining one-record-per-job/statement amplification that can be combined into bounded units. Keep operation ownership, first-original failures, fair scheduling and atomic acknowledgement boundaries. Do not combine unrelated filesystem requests into an acknowledgement-delaying mega-transaction.

## Proof and acceptance

- [ ] Pin the affected source/build/provider/workload identities and classify each candidate as already addressed, rejected or selected from count/profile evidence.
- [ ] State worst-case, amortized and cumulative work in changed keys/bytes, fragmentation, retained generations and concurrent producers; reject quadratic amplification and input-sized resident state.
- [ ] For SQLite changes, retain exact EXPLAIN QUERY PLAN (full EXPLAIN where needed) together with correlated runtime statements, VM steps, rows, pages, bytes, copies and waits. Source inspection or wall time alone is insufficient.
- [ ] Demonstrate identical final content/metadata/namespace, stable capture with later writes, exact Busy/conflict/unknown custody and automatic release/reclamation for affected paths.
- [ ] Keep processing windows bounded and account for all cache, queue, journal/pager, operation-record and physical storage costs. No hidden mutable mirror, helper producer or artificial total file/Commit cap.
- [ ] Any admitted measurement reports speed and storage together, with equal declared/enforced cache state, one sample per selected case/arm, append-only receipts and existing budgets. Reuse unaffected proofs; preserve failed/ineligible/unrun cases. No invented numeric acceptance ceiling.
- [ ] Where mounted Exec or complete live Commit is needed, record its S8/S10 dependency and leave that proof pending until the product path exists. Component observations do not close integrated acceptance.

Each selected implementation follows the existing deepest-file plan, locked scoped build-before-test, bounded test, Clippy/fmt/boundary and exact production-LOC commit rules. Durable builds; all Durable execution remains owner-deferred. No new dependency, third-party patch, automatic retry, host data-path restoration, profile tuning or per-Workspace table-layout redesign is selected by this issue.

## Source observation pin

The inspected repository is the owner's active primary checkout. Source is local-only/unpushed and the main implementation may continue changing it. These file hashes identify the observations; they are not a sealed measured arm. Revalidate only the affected source scope when taking a candidate.

title: Optimize shared WAL Save, partial writes and concurrent cached reads
